column2: 2.4 Portal sustainability

Does the national portal have a strategy to ensure its sustainability?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) provide the URL to this document and (2) describe the main measures to keep the portal running in the long-term and continue to serve its audience
column4: new question
column7: Sustainability is the main driver for many of the architectural and organisational choices made wrt. The national data portal. E.g. in terms of basing the portal on open source CKAN software and interoperable European standards to minimize vendor dependency. Also the decision to harvest metadata from endpoints at the data publishers so that the CKAN could be exhanged for a different data management system, should the need arise.

column4: Not via a dashboard, no, but cf. 111a we monitor the characteristics and quality of metadata on the portal.
column7:
In prioritizing which authorities to onboard to the portal, the most important criterion is the general and specific demand for the data, and the immediate reusability of data (e.g. machine-readable data which is already broadly in use). But to supplement this approach, we also look at which areas of the public sector might not be the most highly profiled, but are nonetheless important to highlight to a broader audience. This has resulted in the recent additions of metadata on data about sports facilities (https://datavejviser.dk/katalog/idraettens-analyseinstitut/05ca477a-8c44-44bc-b336-4bb41e46a825), recommendations from the Danish Council on Climate Change (https://datavejviser.dk/katalog/klimaraadet/99b6a7b5-fdde-4b6c-bf5e-5882a837d327), and, before long, 
The Royal Danish Theatre.

If the question is referring to metadata, then yes, we do summary and specific statistics on the metadata to monitor which datasets are missing certain DCAT-AP attributes.
